newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ANZ JOB ADS SHOWED STEADY DETERIORATION IN JULY.
newsitem.headline: ANZ JOB ADS SHOWED STEADY DETERIORATION IN JULY.

text.p: The trend number of New Zealand job ads fell by 1.2 percent in July following a 1.5 percent drop in June, ANZ Bank said on Tuesday.
In annual terms, the trend number of job ads was down 4.9 percent, the bank said, adding that the number of job ads remained consistently higher than it was during the early 1990s.

"While the decline in job advertising in Wellington and Christchurch has stabilised somewhat over recent months, stronger falls in the monthly number of positions advertised in Auckland are being recorded," the bank said.
The monthly trend in job ads in Auckland dropped 1.1 percent in July, and the trend number of job ads was 2.3 percent lower in July 1997 than in the year-ago month.
Wellington job ads fell by 0.5 percent, following on similar falls in job advertising recorded over the previous three months. There were 11.6 percent fewer ads on a year-ago comparison.
Job advertising in Christchurch fell by 2.2 percent in the month of July and was down 13.5 percent on July 1996.

"The continued decline in job advertisements suggests that an upturn in employment is not yet imminent. Unemployment is likely to rise further over the remainder of 1997, probably reaching around seven percent by the end off the year," the bank said.
In the June quarter household labour force report, reported a week ago, the seasonally-adjusted unemployment rate was 6.7 percent.
